event: Cape Town and KwaZulu-Natal winter storm floods
deaths_text: 5 confirmed by KZN CoGTA; possibly 7 (2 more reported by SABC)
displaced_or_affected: 10,000-15,000 people affected in Western Cape; thousands in KwaZulu-Natal; 400 displaced by a tornado in Ekurhuleni (Gauteng) during the same system
homes_damaged: Philippi: 1,500 structures; Khayelitsha: 800 structures (FloodList). Ekurhuleni tornado: 200 households in Winnie Mandela, 100 shacks and 20 houses in Hospital View
economic_loss: KZN flood damage described as running into millions of rands

notes: FloodList says SAWS issued multiple severe weather warnings (thunderstorms, heavy rain, flooding, strong winds 50-62 km/h) for Western and Northern Cape, but gives no level or lead time. KZN deaths per TimesLIVE: 3 electrocuted in Durban, a woman drowned when her car was washed off a flooded bridge in Chatsworth. Al Jazeera reports Margate got 203 mm in 24 hours and two people missing in KZN. The Gauteng tornado caused no reported deaths (3 minor injuries). Watchers article seen in listing only, not fetched.

event: Johannesburg / Gauteng flash floods (OR Tambo, Alexandra, N3)
deaths_text: 4-6 (SAnews on 10 Nov: four confirmed dead; FloodList/Wikipedia/Africanews: 6)
displaced_or_affected: Close to 200 families lost homes in Setswetla, Alexandra (SAnews); scores homeless and sheltered in churches (FloodList); hundreds rescued; 100-150+ vehicles stranded
homes_damaged: 48+ homes damaged; shacks along Jukskei River banks swept away
economic_loss: Not quantified; insurance claims reported (TimesLIVE 'Storm damage insurance claims pile up after flash floods', cited in AJHTL 2023)
settlement_type_mentioned: informal settlement (Stjwetla, Alexandra township); low-lying suburbs

sources.title: South Africa – Deadly Flash Floods Hit Johannesburg

notes: SAWS recorded about 89 mm in roughly 3 hours; unconfirmed estimates of 90-150 mm in an hour. Four of the deaths came from a truck crash into stranded cars on the N3 (JMPD). A 3-year-old girl went missing in Alexandra. FloodList (12 Nov) says Premier David Makhura intended to declare disaster areas; Wikipedia says Buccleuch was declared a disaster area. The formal gazette was not found, so 'provincial' reflects the stated intent. Mayor Mashaba (SAnews): 'Unfortunately, any severe storm or flash flooding that occurs will result in isolated flooding, as the road infrastructure is not designed for these severities.' The only SAWS warnings found were issued after the event (a severe-thunderstorm watch for 10-12 Nov); no pre-event warning found. The ReliefWeb page was seen in search results only (403 on fetch).

warning_quote: a risk of flash floods in Limpopo, Mpumalanga and Gauteng

event: Ex-Tropical Cyclone Dineo and persistent rain floods (North West, KZN, Mpumalanga, Limpopo)
deaths_text: at least 3 (a boy drowned crossing a stream in Loporung; 2 died when their vehicle was swept away in Lemenong)
homes_damaged: About 20 houses damaged in Mpumalanga and 5 in Limpopo (Watchers); a house collapse in iLembe injured 4
warning_lead_time: Government alert issued 15 Feb 2017 ahead of the expected 16-19 Feb storm period (about 1 day ahead of landfall impacts)
warning_quote: Abandon your home immediately guided by relevant authorities if evacuation is recommended, before access is cut off by flood water.

Government calls communities to be on high alert ahead of arrival of Tropical Cyclone Dineo
sources.publisher: South African Government (Dept of Cooperative Governance)

sources.title: PICS: Heavy rain, flooding as ex-Dineo sweeps over SA

notes: The government alert (15 Feb) warned of winds up to 150 km/h and up to 200 mm of rain in 24 hours for Limpopo, Mpumalanga and northern KZN (Vhembe, Mopani, Waterberg, Ehlanzeni, Kruger NP). The deaths actually recorded were in North West, which was not the main warned area. A woman and a 15-month-old baby went missing on 23 Feb in the Mafodobo River: FloodList lists it with the North West incidents, while Watchers places it in KZN, so the location is conflicting. The N12 through Wolmaransstad was closed. The rains helped end the drought, with the Vaal Dam near full.

sources.title: South Africa – Hundreds Evacuated, 1 Feared Dead After Floods in KwaZulu-Natal

notes: 24-hour rainfall to 15 May: Mandini 133 mm, Charters Creek 125 mm, Durban Airport 101 mm. Sources cited in the article: KZN CoGTA, SAWS, KZN EMS, SABC. The preventive evacuation at Mzingwenya suggests some anticipatory action, but no warning wording was reported.

event: Cape storm (worst winter storm in 30 years) with Cape Town flooding
deaths_text: at least 8 storm-related (plus 7 in the Knysna fires the storm winds fanned; 15 total per Wikipedia); Al Jazeera: 'at least nine' in some reports
displaced_or_affected: Thousands left homeless in informal settlements; 8,000-10,000 evacuated, mainly because of the Knysna fires
homes_damaged: About 700-800 homes/structures flooded in Cape Town; 135 schools damaged; about 600 structures destroyed by fire in Knysna/Plettenberg Bay
economic_loss: Fire damage R4-5.1 billion to private property plus R136 million to public infrastructure (Wikipedia; fire-related, not flood)
warning_lead_time: Severe weather warnings issued Tuesday 6 June 2017, about 1 day before landfall on 7 June; storm forecast days ahead ('Cape Town braces for major winter storm')
warning_quote: Residents should make real preparations for the storm and not take it lightly

notes: Most deaths were not from drowning: 4 (a family) died in a lightning-caused fire in Kraaifontein, 1 in a building collapse in Lavender Hill, and 3 in a fire in Rheenendal. Include with caution if analysis is restricted to flood deaths. Resident quote from Al Jazeera (fear, not about warnings): 'I'm scared to stay in my house because of wind. Also the rain, that's why I moved here with my child. We're scared to stay in my shack' (Unati Sigcau). Warning quote is from SAWS communications manager Hannelee Doubell (Watchers, 6 June). IFRC launched DREF MDRZA007 (CHF 140,855) on 19 June 2017; the ReliefWeb page was seen in search results only (403 on fetch). Wind gusts about 120 km/h; waves 9-12 m. The storm came about two weeks after a drought disaster declaration.

event: Durban / KZN supercell storm and record-rain floods
displaced_or_affected: About 500 people displaced across the province; displaced people sheltered in community halls such as Montclair Community Hall
homes_damaged: Dozens of buildings damaged; 19 collapsed buildings and perimeter walls; flooded households; around 300 schools affected (Watchers)
economic_loss: Damages estimated to run into millions of rand (KZN government)
warning_lead_time: SAWS said warnings were issued as early as Sunday (8 Oct), about 2 days ahead, and sent to provincial disaster management and municipalities; eThekwini's first public warning reportedly came at 10am on the storm day, after the storm had started
warning_quote: the warnings were issued but the vast majority of ordinary citizens did not receive this critical life saving info

sources.title: South Africa – Storm Leaves 8 Dead, Record Rain in Durban
KwaZulu-Natal on impact of mega-storm
KZN storm: Tragedy, displays of bravery and acts of compassion when floods hit
#SAStorms: Light thunderstorms expected for KZN - AS IT HAPPENED
Several dead in massive South Africa storm, Johannesburg hit hard
Durban, South Africa receives record-breaking rain, 8 people dead
EThekwini disaster plan 'a disaster'

notes: Durban had a record 108 mm in 24 hours (previous record 105 mm, October 1985); Paddock had 144 mm. Deaths include a 19-month-old baby swept away in Umlazi, 2 patients killed by a wall collapse at Prince Mshiyeni Hospital, a 12-year-old boy drowned at Izingolweni, an 8-year-old girl struck by lightning, 2 deaths in Nquthu and a driver in Isipingo. A police officer was also killed by a falling container (IOL). The warning quote is News24's live-blog rendering of SAWS CEO Jerry Lengoasa's remarks; News24 also reported 'the Durban radar was not working due to system breakdown at the time of the storm' and that four radars were not working. The claim that the city's first warning came at 10am rests on search snippets of the Mercury article (PressReader returned 403); treat it as medium confidence. KZN government: 'At this stage, we cannot confirm a formal declaration of disaster as processes are underway.' The same supercell system caused hail and flooding in Johannesburg on 9-10 Oct. Resident quote (TimesLIVE, about the rescue, not about warnings): 'I went inside and I got the baby and I carried her out of the water...The water just came and took the baby.'

displaced_or_affected: Some homes evacuated in northern Johannesburg

notes: SAWS: Pretoria 145 mm and Johannesburg 117 mm in 24 hours to 23 March (the March average for Johannesburg is about 90 mm). sources.title: Two drownings under investigation as flash floods hit Pretoria
Flash floods on Gauteng roads as rains persist

notes: Both sources are from the same publisher. Search and rescue was suspended because of dangerous conditions; I found no follow-up confirming the deaths. Officials gave standard safety advice, e.g. 'Never drive on a road that is totally covered by water and no road surface can be seen' and 'All low-lying bridges must be avoided during a flood'. There were widespread power outages across all seven Tshwane regions.
